inside_destinations.detail: West Coast Tasmania 10, Franklin-Gordon Wild Rivers National Park 4, Southwest National Park 3 (all in proposed destinations; no existing Tasmanian destination)

standalone.note: First five are re-homed if tas-northwest-cradle proposes a Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair destination.

new_destinations: Southwest National Park (3, flagship exemption: owner to accept or make standalone)

stronger_left_out.name: Takayna / Tarkine
stronger_left_out.reason: Region-scale; duplicate of the north-west pass

stronger_left_out.name: Rosebery
stronger_left_out.reason: Town as base with services; for: the surviving mining community

stronger_left_out.name: Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area
stronger_left_out.reason: A designation covering a fifth of Tasmania, not a single place to go; the parks inside it are the spots

stronger_left_out.name: West Coast Wilderness Railway
stronger_left_out.reason: Case for: heritage rack railway with no single destination (the journey is the draw), 2 sources; against: an operator ticket and the places at its ends are the spots

stronger_left_out.name: Port Davey
stronger_left_out.reason: Remote; access only by boat or flight

stronger_left_out.name: Hells Gates
stronger_left_out.reason: Entrance headland to Macquarie Harbour, seen only from Gordon River cruises (Wikivoyage Strahan lists it inside the cruise description); no public place to stand, so rule 2 fails and it is part of the cruise experience.

stronger_left_out.name: Strathgordon
stronger_left_out.reason: A hydro settlement beside its attraction (Gordon Dam); wrapper

stronger_left_out.name: Tullah
stronger_left_out.reason: Case against: a town is a spot only if the town is a draw, and its draws are the dam and a weekend-only railway, which are better as their own spots; case for: a few things to do and two counted sources. Judge Mackintosh Dam and Wee Georgie Wood Railway separately.

stronger_left_out.name: Maydena
stronger_left_out.reason: Small base town outside the park with no sourced draw of its own

stronger_left_out.name: Melaleuca
stronger_left_out.reason: Reachable only by plane or multi-day walk

stronger_left_out.name: Wilderness Air
stronger_left_out.reason: Scenic flight operator, not a place

stronger_left_out.name: Arthur River
stronger_left_out.reason: Town wrapper near its attraction; for: the field centre and river cruises (not sourced)

stronger_left_out.name: Kutikina Cave
stronger_left_out.reason: Archaeological cave with restricted access; nothing a visitor can do or see (rule 2)

stronger_left_out.name: Corinna
stronger_left_out.reason: Case for: historic Huon pine settlement, Pieman River cruise and a base for the Tarkine. Against: its draw is access to the Tarkine (the ferry is a vehicle), one real source, visit mostly a stopover; a town is a spot only if it is a draw itself.

stronger_left_out.name: Derwent Bridge
stronger_left_out.reason: A village beside its own attraction (the Wall) is a wrapper; keep the Wall, mention the village in a description

stronger_left_out.name: King River
stronger_left_out.reason: One tourism-board mention, no visitor listing for a site

stronger_left_out.name: Lyell Highway
stronger_left_out.reason: A road/route, not a place (COVERAGE: a spot is a place)

stronger_left_out.name: The Ship That Never Was
stronger_left_out.reason: A recurring theatre show, not a permanent place (rule 4)

stronger_left_out.name: Gordon River Road
stronger_left_out.reason: A road, not a place

stronger_left_out.name: Cape Sorell Lighthouse
stronger_left_out.reason: Exterior-only, remote (boat/4WD); for: a named landmark in the guide's See list

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Tyndall
stronger_left_out.reason: No counted source found; a web search shows only walkers' forums and a planned 2029 Iconic Walk

strongest_outsiders: Standalone kept by views: Lake St Clair 63038 (Michigan figure, unreliable), Mount Ossa 18955, Overland Track 12552. Strongest left out (all outside kept spans): West Coast Wilderness Railway 6803 (review), Rosebery 9232 (review), Takayna / Tarkine 9708 (review), Port Davey 3856 (review), Hells Gates 3738 (reject, rule 2).
benchmark: Not applicable to Tasmania (NZ benchmark list); no TSS Earnslaw-type vehicle spot proposed (the railway, cruises and Corinna ferry are review or rejected as vehicles); negative benchmark logic held (festival/theatre show rejected).
notes: All left-out items above have a concrete rule reason (vehicle/operator, remote with no access, wrapper town, not a place, one source). Views for Lake St Clair, Gordon River, Hogarth Falls and others come from candidates.json and some belong to other places (Lake St Clair's is Michigan's). Views of 0 mean no article or redirect; the kept spots Hogarth Falls, Gordon River, Donaghys Hill, Wall, Edge of the World have 0, so no candidate with views is 'weaker than the lowest'.
